title: Kamala Harris warns window closing for AI safeguards, urges US-China cooperation
key_facts: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris urged governments and technology companies on Wednesday 14 Oct to put AI safeguards in place urgently, warning the window for containing the gravest risks was closing.
She spoke at South Korea's Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul.
She named three existential dangers from AI: cybersecurity threats, AI-enabled weapons and systems escaping human control.
She urged the United States to engage China on international AI rules and standards, saying rivalry should not preclude cooperation on shared risks.
She criticised President Trump's 'erratic tariffs' and warned against a transactional approach that cost the US global influence.
She has been campaigning for Democratic candidates before the 2026 midterm elections and said of a 2028 run: 'I'm still thinking about it. I haven't decided yet.'
quote_evidence: 'If we are to have any guardrails and safeguards, they have to be at the table,' Harris said of AI developers.
'My concern is that the window is shutting.'
'There is room for cooperation where our interests are aligned,' Harris said.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible 2028 presidential candidate sets out Democratic positions on AI safety and China cooperation, though she holds no office.
